svg.text: The reset / boot plunger, fitted in the case
Renders of the real geometry — the case sliced around the two switch openings (grey) with the plunger pair in place (green).
Both come out of the same btn_* modules in parts/case/case_polykybd_split72_lr.scad, so the part and the hole cannot drift apart.
A — from outside
the two noses sit flush in the wall, 0.12 mm all round
B — from inside
the board (blue) is translucent here; the ears stop 0.4 mm under it
C — section on the left button centreline
switch (amber) on the board underside, from its datasheet box
D — the part on its own
one part per half: two plungers, a 0.8 × 1.2 mm bar, 1.6 mm posts
and only as good as the print tolerance. Verified by parts/case/check_btn_plunger.py (12 checks).
Unlike the bonded LED inserts the protection here is DIMENSIONAL: it is the 0.12 mm sliding gap,
against the ~2.5 N its own switch needs.
Pressing one plunger bends the 1.6 mm-anchored beam between them, so about 0.16 N reaches the other,
the ears against the shoulder, which is what keeps the noses flush with the outer face.
and locates the part, then the two noses push out through the wall. The switch’s own return spring holds
Fitted from the inside before the board goes in: the bar drops into the slot along the bottom of the pocket
a notch at the top of the nose would widen the one gap the part exists to close.
0.4 mm under it. The nose is deliberately NOT capped: it is in the wall, which carries on above the ledge, and
inboard of the wall at the opening’s full height stands in its seat — the ears did, by 0.48 mm. They now stop
